title: The Ledger of Ashcombe
premise: When August Blackwood exhumes the coffin of Ashcombe's founder, Ezekiel Crane, and finds it empty, he discovers a ledger in the crypt listing payments made to a living witness everyone believes died fifteen years ago. As August follows the ledger's paper trail, he uncovers that the town's founding families have been funding an annual 'anniversary dinner' to keep one man — the true heir, hidden in plain sight as the town handyman — silent about a murder that built their fortune. The climax comes at the anniversary dinner itself, where August forces a public confession using the ledger and the witness's own testimony. In the end, justice arrives outside any courtroom: the families' power collapses, August adopts the witness into his quiet household, and Ashcombe begins burying its secrets for good.
about_author: Isandro Blackwood is the pen name of a former small-town records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing other people's unfinished business before turning it into fiction. He writes mysteries about institutions, inheritance, and the quiet violence of respectable places.

chapters.title: The Empty Man
chapters.summary: August Blackwood's POV. A court order forces August to exhume founder Ezekiel Crane for a property dispute, and he opens the coffin himself to find it empty except for a fresh-cut sprig of ash. The town council demands discretion; August, who has filed every death in Ashcombe for fifteen years, feels his orderly world tilt. Emotional beat: dread beneath professional calm.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Alphabet
chapters.summary: August's POV. Searching his records, August realizes Crane's official death certificate is a forgery — signed by his own predecessor, who drowned conveniently soon after. He finds a second ledger hidden in the crypt wall: fifteen years of payments from the founding families to an unnamed recipient. Emotional beat: the horror of realizing his beloved archive was someone's accomplice.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with councilwoman Vivian Marsh. The founding families prepare the annual Founder's Dinner while quietly pressuring August to close the exhumation as vandalism. Vivian's chapters reveal she knows more than she says and fears someone within her own circle. Emotional beat: polite menace; the reader sees the machinery of respectability working.

chapters.title: A Grave That Isn't His
chapters.summary: August's POV. Following the ledger's delivery route, August finds the payments were collected at the grave of Daniel Reeve — the young man officially dead these fifteen years, supposedly the drunk driver who killed Crane's son. But the headstone's soil is turned every month. Someone tends it. Someone collects there. Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Handyman
chapters.summary: August's POV. August confronts Silas Wren, the town handyman who has repaired every porch in Ashcombe for fifteen years and never aged past forty in anyone's memory. Silas denies everything, but August notices the man's hands shake at the mention of the dinner. That night, August's office is ransacked and the ledger stolen. Emotional beat: isolation — the first friend-shaped suspect.

chapters.title: What the Son Saw
chapters.summary: Vivian's POV. Flashback threads reveal the truth: Crane's son wasn't killed by Daniel Reeve — he was killed by Crane himself after witnessing the founder's embezzlement that drowned three workers, and Reeve was framed, then 'died' on paper to become the town's permanent hostage. Vivian, then a young clerk, helped forge it and has paid ever since. Emotional beat: complicity and its slow rot.

chapters.title: Ashes in the Wall
chapters.summary: August's POV. August recovers a duplicate page from his predecessor's effects: proof the coffin was emptied the night of the funeral because Crane couldn't bear to bury his son's secret with a stranger's body — or because the body was never Crane's son at all. August realizes the empty coffin holds Crane's actual remains, moved to hide how he really died. Emotional beat: revelation reframing everything.

chapters.title: Silence, Purchased Annually
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Days before the dinner, Silas disappears, and Vivian finds the families voting to make August the next name in the ledger — a payment to him, or a price on him. She slips August the original minutes of the night Reeve was framed. Emotional beat: betrayal inside the conspiracy; Vivian choosing a side at last.

chapters.title: The Toast
chapters.summary: August's POV, climax. At the Founder's Dinner, August stands during the toast and reads the ledger aloud, then brings in Silas — alive, hiding in the crypt where he's lived among the dead rather than among the living. Before the whole town, Silas testifies to what he saw fifteen years ago. The families fracture; one confesses to save herself. Emotional beat: catharsis — the quiet man finally speaks over the powerful.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: August's POV, resolution. Months later, the founders face ruin and partial justice — no trial can fully reach what they did, but exposure strips them of everything the law cannot. August reburies the true remains under a new stone bearing both names, and Silas moves into the room above August's garage. The ledger goes into the archive, alphabetized under T for truth. Emotional beat: found family, and peace hard-won.
